title: Mitigate tenant-burst-induced scheduling oscillations causing small-request starvation
creator: Marco Delgado
description: Summary: Multiple customer escalations (ScribePay on Hosted, MediLens on Private VPC) reported sudden latency spikes for short prompt requests and persistent tail latency during multi-tenant bursts. Investigation shows an interaction between the adaptive admission window, tenant-level weight drift during Dedicated pool rebalances, and aggressive KV cache eviction: the scheduler oscillates between admitting large long-context batches and starving small low-latency requests. This manifests as queue starvation for short requests and amplification of long-context tail latencies.
problem_statement: When one or more tenants issue microbursts of long-context generation, adaptive admission heuristics expand batch windows and prefer throughput-optimal batches. After a pool rebalanced or a Dedicated capacity change, tenant weight estimates drift and hysteresis is insufficient, causing the admission window to repeatedly oscillate. Long requests hold KV cache and GPU resources longer, and short requests are forced to wait behind repeatedly created throughput batches resulting in 95th/99th percentile regressions for latency-sensitive customers.
impact_details: Observed impacts: (1) ScribePay reported 3 production incidents over 48 hours with 99th percentile latency jumping from ~120ms to >1.2s for short requests; business-critical chat flows timed out. (2) MediLens (Private) saw degraded SLAs during a scheduled Dedicated capacity upgrade when tenant weights recalculated. Affected customers experienced timeouts and automatic client failovers. Internal metrics show increased batch fill times, KV eviction spikes, and tenant admission oscillation traces in the scheduler logs.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause is combinatorial: (a) adaptive admission window increases to favor throughput once queued tokens exceed threshold; (b) long-context requests hold KV cache and extend per-batch GPU occupancy; (c) tenant weight recalculation after pool rebalancing misestimates active low-latency tenants, removing protective bias; and (d) hysteresis in the admission algorithm is static and tuned for steady-state, not bursty multi-tenant rebalances. Together these cause rapid state flips in the scheduler (oscillation), leading to starvation of small requests.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy a Dedicated pool with 3 tenants: A (low-latency), B (steady), C (bursting long-context). 2) Warm models until KV caches reach normal occupancy. 3) Emit a microburst of long-context requests from tenant C while rebalancer triggers a pool resize. 4) Observe admission window growth, repeated long batches, and suppressed admission for tenant A’s short requests. 5) Capture scheduler traces and GPU occupancy; telemetry replicates production graphs.
proposed_fix: Implement three coordinated mitigations: (1) Dynamic hysteresis for admission window: make hysteresis scale with recent variance in batch fill times and pool-rebalance events instead of a static timer. (2) Tenant burst token bucket: track short-request tokens per tenant that protect a small low-latency admission path even during throughput-favoring windows. Tokens refill at per-tenant rates and are consumed by short requests. (3) Preemptive small-request slot reservation: reserve a bounded number of per-GPU slots for low-latency flows and allow preemption of queued long-context requests when starvation is detected. Add feature flags to enable per-deployment tuning for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
rollback_plan: Feature-flag controlled rollout. If regressions appear, flip flag to disable dynamic hysteresis and return to static behavior. For token-bucket/preemption, we can reduce reservation to 0 to fully disable without rolling back scheduler binary. Emergency route: drain to read-only capacity and divert traffic to fallback model variant (smaller context) per current failure mode runbook.
qa_and_test_plan: Unit tests for admission logic, integration tests in the scheduler simulator with deterministic replay harness (replay traces from ScribePay incident), and e2e canary in staging with synthetic burst traffic. Metrics: 50/95/99 p50/p95/p99 latency, batch fill time distribution, KV eviction rate, admission flip count per minute. Add new automatic assertions for admission flip rate and short-request starvation ratio.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and enable behind feature flag in a single-pod canary in staging. 2) Run 24-hour deterministic replay and synthetic burst scenarios. 3) Canary in Hosted with 1% traffic for 6 hours, monitor SLOs. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with additional Dedicated pool canaries. 5) For Private customers, provide opt-in package and recommended knob values; push to MediLens staging first before customer production.
monitoring_and_alerts: New dashboards: 'admission-window-hysteresis', 'tenant-token-usage', 'preemption-events'. Alerts: high admission flip rate (>10 flips/min sustained), small-request starvation ratio > 0.05 for >5m, KV eviction spikes correlated with admission events. Tie alerts to PagerDuty escalation playbook created in incident-2345.
postmortem_actions: 1) Ship fixes and run 2-week observation window. 2) Update runbooks for Dedicated pool upgrades to pause tenant weight recalculation during live traffic increases. 3) Add pre-migration simulation step to predict admission stability. 4) Documentation: Confluence page with operational knobs and recommended values per deployment type.
